clue.text: Comes from the East and takes the car about

indicators.note: about means round, so the driving word goes around the compass point

parts.note: to take the car is to drive, so this gives drives
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Someone arrives from the east and drives the car around.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive from a place or source is to come from it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Wasn't "23 _____, 10 (without negative) 24 to 24 been 17" a 3 19?

definitions.meaning: was not in being: had no existence
the blank in a Voltaire-style quotation, 'If God ... he would have to have been invented', using other lights' answers

explanation.walkthrough: The second half fills the blank in Voltaire's maxim, 'If God did not exist, it would be necessary to invent him', built from 23, 10 minus its negative, 24 twice, and 17.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking existence is the plain meaning of the negative past tense of being.

clue.text: You are upset and so is left-winger

indicators.note: upset means the letters of are are knocked over and rearranged
and so is says the next word is upset too, turned upward in this down clue

parts.note: a red is a left-wing politician

explanation.surface: You are upset, and so is a left-wing campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles ARE to REA; 'and so is' upsets RED as well, read upwards as DER.
explanation.definitionFit: The person reading the clue is addressed as you, so the word for whoever reads names you.

clue.text: Sceptical French placing West African lake on New Guinea

parts.note: Lake Volta is the great reservoir in Ghana
Irian is the Indonesian name for New Guinea, as in Irian Jaya

explanation.surface: A doubting Frenchman sets a Ghanaian lake on top of a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the lake above the island name.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Voltaire, the French writer, were known for religious scepticism, so the adjective names that French sceptical outlook.

clue.text: The school doctor's a fool

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: The school doctor turns out to be an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A schmo is American slang, from Yiddish, for a stupid or contemptible person.

clue.text: Ambiguous form of help in back yard?

indicators.note: in places the rearranged word inside the reversed police letters
back means the police department letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Scotland Yard is home to the CID, the Criminal Investigation Department

indicators.note: form of means a new shape of the letters of help

explanation.surface: Is a reshuffled form of help hidden in the back yard puzzling?
explanation.walkthrough: 'back yard' reads as a garden, but 'Yard' is Scotland Yard, London police headquarters, and 'back' turns its detectives' initials round; 'form of' rearranges the helping word inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Delphic oracle gave notoriously double-edged answers, so the word means obscure or open to two readings.

clue.text: Ground floor row and its consequence

indicators.note: a consequence is what results from something, so the letters before it come out in a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A ground floor quarrel and what follows from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consequence' asks for what the letters of ROW AND ITS turn into.
explanation.definitionFit: Downstair, as an adjective, describes the lower or ground floor of a house.

clue.text: Praise was axed

explanation.walkthrough: Archbishop Laud, Charles I's churchman, was executed by the axe on Tower Hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Laud is a verb meaning extol, and also the surname of a beheaded archbishop.

clue.text: See 23
Sword encompasses grand upper-class

indicators.note: encompasses means the sword word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a cutlass is a short curved sword
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A sword surrounds a posh fellow's grand.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-glass accent is a very refined, upper-class way of speaking.

clue.text: Do art student's protracted speech

parts.note: to do art is to draw
L, for learner, is a student

explanation.surface: An art student's slow way of talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is slow speech with drawn-out vowels.

clue.text: See 23
Fast mover on river backed by another feature of Sydney

indicators.note: backed means the hare and the Italian river are read in reverse

parts.note: a hare is a fast-running animal
the Po is the river of northern Italy
another river, here the Ouse, a common English river name

explanation.surface: A speedy creature on a river, with another river behind it, makes a Sydney landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns HARE PO into OPERAH; 'by another' adds a second river, the Ouse, a river in Yorkshire and elsewhere in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sydney Opera House, with its sail-like roofs, is the city's best-known landmark.

clue.text: King (early English) and partner turn turtle

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
EE stands for Early English, the medieval architectural style
a lover is a romantic partner

explanation.surface: A king, an early Englishman and his partner capsize.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn turtle is to capsize, and to keel over is to fall over sideways.

clue.text: Royal house takes Manx town with zest

parts.note: the House of Orange, as in William of Orange, is a royal dynasty
Peel is a town on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A royal dynasty acquires a town on the Isle of Man with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with zest' reads as eagerness, but zest is the coloured rind of citrus.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is the grated outer skin of a citrus fruit used in cooking.

clue.text: See 23
Roman historian gets fat on first Guardian

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat
I is the Roman numeral one, hence first
this newspaper speaking of itself is us

explanation.surface: A Roman historian puts on weight reading the Guardian first.
explanation.definitionFit: Suetonius wrote The Twelve Caesars, so he is a historian of Rome.

clue.text: See 23
See 23
Satisfied expression in the midst of poverty retained by notorious firm which has many faces

indicators.note: retained by means the firm's name holds the rest inside it

parts.note: Enron was the energy company that collapsed in an accounting scandal

indicators.note: in the midst of puts the exclamation in the middle of the poverty word

parts.note: need is poverty or want
ah is a sigh of satisfaction

explanation.surface: A contented sigh amid hardship, held by a scandalous firm with many faces.
explanation.definitionFit: A solid with nine plane faces is a polyhedron, so it has many faces.

clue.text: Saw Chinese principle lose tension outside

indicators.note: outside means the drooping word goes round the Chinese term

parts.note: to sag is to slacken, losing tension
yin is the passive principle of Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: A Chinese philosophical principle goes slack all round.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb, a traditional piece of wisdom.

clue.text: Group of palindromes

parts.note: a six-line stanza whose name splits into two three-letter words each reading the same both ways

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a poetic group, and its first and second halves each read the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestet is a group of six lines, the closing part of a sonnet.

clue.text: See 12
Loudly call out number, if there's time during election

indicators.note: during means the middle pieces sit within the election word

parts.note: a vote is an election
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone shouts a number during an election, if there is time.
explanation.definitionFit: To vociferate is to shout or clamour noisily.

clue.text: Awfully fat woman designed a house that revolved around t' kitchen — not me: I'm for eating out, as the 19 goes

definitions.text: I'm for eating out, as the 19 goes

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the long run of words is rearranged

parts.words: fat woman designed a house that revolved around t' kitchen
parts.note: the bulk of the fodder
these words join the fodder too

explanation.surface: A large woman designed a kitchen-centred house, but the speaker prefers restaurants, as the proverb says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' scrambles all the words from fat to me; the definition is a summary of the quip, attributed to Fran Lebowitz. 19 is SAYING.
explanation.definitionFit: The quip says the speaker was not meant to cook, so they eat out, which is what the definition sums up.

clue.text: See 23
Successfully confronting, not in the house opposite

parts.note: out means not at home
facing means opposite

explanation.surface: Someone stands up to the house across the road while away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Outfacing someone is defeating them by confronting them boldly.

clue.text: See 1 down
Reins in about five hundred in notes

indicators.note: the second in puts the inner piece inside the musical notes

parts.note: keys are musical notes or tonalities

indicators.note: about means the word in goes around the numeral

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Reins are tucked into five hundred banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: Reins in the Bible means the kidneys, seat of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins is an archaic word for the kidneys or loins, from Latin renes.

clue.text: Happiness is to be about half well dressed

indicators.note: about means the dressed word goes round the inner letters

parts.note: dight is an archaic word for dressed or adorned

indicators.note: half here takes the middle half of the four-letter word, losing its outer letters

explanation.surface: Happiness is going to be about half as well dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The two middle letters of WELL, E and L, are half the word; they go inside DIGHT. 'is to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight is great pleasure or joy, a synonym of happiness.
